g.text: HOT PATH — RAM only, zero disk I/O

ul.li: visited set — generation-stamped array, not a map[int]struct{}. Clearing is gen++, O(1), no alloc.
heaps — plain []candidate with hand-written sift up/down. container/heap passes values as any, which boxes every candidate (~795 allocs/search).
The only two allocations are the result slice and the []Result handed back to the caller.

div.p: This scratch is per-traversal, not graph-owned. It comes from a pooled searchState, which is what lets Search hold only RLock and run in parallel — graph-owned buffers would make concurrent searches corrupt each other.
ef is the only per-query knob. Bigger = wider layer-0 search = higher recall, slower. Locked baselines: recall@10 = 0.999 at dim 32, 0.972 at dim 768, measured against brute force in graph_test.go.
M and EfConstruction are build-time and structural — changing M requires a full rebuild.
len(query) == cfg.Dimension if ef < k { ef = k } — ef below k cannot return k results empty graph → nil, nil
Into st.queryBuf, scratch borrowed from the pool — the caller's slice is never touched, and this costs no allocation
searchLayer returns ascending by distance, so this is a slice: w[:k]
k reads, not hundreds. This is the only disk access in the entire query, and it is for text/metadata — never for the float32s the traversal needed.

div.h3: "Get indices from HNSW, then fetch vectors from disk"
div.p: This cannot work. The graph does not produce candidates and then need vectors — it needs a vector at every hop to compute the next distance. At ef=64 that is hundreds of lookups per query.
Making traversal disk-friendly is DiskANN — a different index, deliberately out of scope for v1.
At each layer, step to the closest neighbor until none improves. ef=1. Cheap navigation that lands us in the right region.
Best-first search on layer 0, the only layer holding every vector.
candidates — min-heap (closest first) results — max-heap (farthest at top, so the worst keeper is O(1) to test)
Stop when the nearest frontier node is farther than the current worst result: everything left is worse too.
